name: Tolerex
description: A broad-spectrum immunosuppressant specifically engineered to prevent the adaptive immune system from targeting cyberware alloys, synthetic polymers, and interface ports. Tolerex works by selectively downregulating the macrophage response to non-biological implant materials while leaving pathogen defense largely intact. Missing even two consecutive doses can trigger acute chrome rejection, characterized by swelling, interface port inflammation, and in severe cases, implant expulsion.
side_effects: nausea during first two weeks of use
rare: opportunistic fungal infections in heavy-augment users
yellowing of sclera with decade-long use
street_price: Φ12–Φ40 per week depending on formulation
cultural_context: Tolerex or a generic equivalent is taken by the majority of augmented adults in GLMZ — estimates suggest 60–70% of the population. It is so mundane it has no mystique. Shelf dwellers buy gray-market generics cut with filler; Spire residents get custom-compounded monthly infusions. Missing your Tol is a social embarrassment, like forgetting to eat. Street medics keep it in bulk.
story_hooks: A Shelf chemist has been selling counterfeit Tolerex — identical packaging, inert filler — and a wave of rejection cases is hitting Tier 1 clinics, but tracing the supply chain means confronting someone who has protection from above.

A corporate runner discovers their employer has been quietly substituting their Tolerex with a proprietary formulation that also logs biometric data through their chrome — every heartbeat, every location, every stress response.
Someone is hoarding Tolerex ahead of a predicted supply disruption, and the price spike on the Shelf is already killing people who can't afford to skip doses.
